tier_reason: Tier C stands; correction from the enricher's code reading: the '5.0x to BGRX' row (24.7 ms) does not time the shipped decoder. nj_decode_bgrx exists only under -DNJ_REFERENCE and calls the old engine (libjpeg-turbo decodes bands, upsamples and converts colour); it is not exported in libnitro.map and the public API outputs YUV planes only. Valid like-for-like figures are 1.04x on one thread and 9.2x on 16 threads, both to YUV planes. bench/pngbench divides by all files, so unsupported PNGs (palette, 16-bit, interlaced) count near 0 ms for nitropng while Wuffs decodes them.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Intel i9 13th gen, 50 private camera JPEGs, bench/bench decode-only from memory (bench/results/results.txt). Like-for-like on one thread: nitrojpeg to YUV planes 103.0 ms/image versus libjpeg-turbo 3.1.2 to YUV planes 107.4 ms (1.04x, derived from page data). All 16 threads versus libjpeg-turbo on one thread: nitrojpeg to YUV 11.7 ms versus 107.4 ms (9.2x, derived). The BGRX row (24.7 ms versus 124.1 ms, 5.0x) times an unshipped NJ_REFERENCE path built on libjpeg-turbo and is not a figure for the public API, which outputs YUV planes only. Apple M1 (43 photos, bench/results/m1.txt): one thread 153.8 versus 168.1 ms (1.09x, derived), 8 threads 30.4 versus 168.1 ms (5.5x). PNG: nitropng parallel versus Wuffs to BGRA on 34 PNGs, with unsupported files counted near 0 ms for nitropng.

tier_reason: Tier B stands as an independent third-party measurement, but the enricher found the measured code is gone: the gist times SkBitmapScaler from Skia m53 (SSE2-only, int16 14-bit fixed-point convolver), which was deleted from Skia on 2017-07-20 ('Assume HQ is handled by pipeline, delete legacy code-path'). Current scalePixels is raster-pipeline sampling (linear or fixed 4x4 cubic, no Lanczos, cubic cannot use mipmaps), so the numbers describe no Skia since 2017. The harness is also asymmetric: the Skia side preallocates the destination outside the timed loop on a white N32 source, while the ImageMagick side pays a clone, a new image and Python Wand overhead per call; Pillow-SIMD 4.3 AVX2 needed 0.32-0.54x of Skia's time on the same data.

corrections.caveats: Stale: the timed SkBitmapScaler (Skia m53, 2016, SSE2-only fixed-point convolver) was deleted from Skia on 2017-07-20; current Skia resampling is raster-pipeline linear or 4x4 cubic with no Lanczos, so these numbers describe no Skia built since 2017. Baseline is ImageMagick 6.8.9-9. Harness asymmetry favours Skia: destination preallocated outside the timed loop and a white N32 source, while ImageMagick pays clone, new image and Python Wand overhead per call. Pillow-SIMD 4.3 AVX2 needed 0.32-0.54x of Skia's time on the same data. Skia now needs C++20 and strongly prefers Clang.
